newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesian LSWR supplies seen tight in July.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian LSWR supplies seen tight in July.

text.p: The low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) supplies from Indonesia are expected to be reduced in July partly due to the shutdown of a refinery for maintenance, traders said on Thursday.

With imminent summer demand from Japan and tightening supplies, traders said they expected LSWR prices to edge up to $16.00 per barrel, free-on-board Indonesia, towards the end of the month from the current $15.50 per barrel.
LSWR prices hovered just above $15.00 per barrel in the past two months.

A Japanese trader said Indonesia's state oil firm Pertamina is expected to allocate between 2.5 and 3.0 million barrels of LSWR in July, down from the total of 3.6 million that was exported in June including barrels rolled over from May.
In May, it allocated 3.85 million barrels, with 500,000 barrels rolled over from April.
Pertamina is expected to shut down some units in the 200,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Balikpapan refinery for maintenance from July 10 for 32 days, cutting its LSWR output, traders said.
"In any case, supplies will be lower than three million barrels in July," the Japanese trader said.
"Japan has started to prepare for the summer demand. I think the buying should start at the end of the month or in early July," he said.
A Singapore trader said he saw support for LSWR at above $15.50 per barrel in the near term.
